description: Financial astrology sky analogues (matching skies): find the past or future dates whose planetary positions best match a reference sky (a moment, now, or positions you give), ranked by a stated angular distance, for backtests and research. Matching skies by geometry, data only: give a reference (a UTC moment, 'now', or your own positions) and get the dates in a range (past, future or both, 1800-2200, 1h..1w grid) whose sky is closest, ranked by a weighted mean of circular longitude differences (geocentric and/or heliocentric), pair angles (aspects), declination differences and retrograde-flag mismatches, in degrees. Each match gives its date, unix timestamp, score, every body's exact longitude and retrograde flag and each feature's distance, in columns ready for pandas. The metric formula is in the response; the same request returns the same bytes and hash, future dates included. Up to 100 matches and 36,600 candidate dates per call; no market data. Data for your own analysis — never a signal or forecast. Deterministic (JPL DE440, no LLM); every result carries meta.result_sha256. Price $0.25 per call via REST POST https://astro-agent.dev/v1/finance/analogues (x402 or MPP); always paid, never a free call.

bodies.description: Bodies to match. Default: Sun..Pluto (geo), Mercury..Pluto with Earth (helio).

direction.description: Search before the reference, after it, or both (default; the only choice with reference.values, which has no time).

features.description: What to compare: 'longitude' (default), 'aspects' (the angle between every pair of bodies), 'declination', 'retrograde' (geocentric flags, Mercury..Pluto).

max_distance.description: Optional: only matches whose score (degrees) is at most this.

min_separation_days.description: Minimum gap between two matches and between a match and the reference time, so one passage gives one match. Raise it (e.g. 3650) to skip the current cycle of slow planets.

perspective.description: Positions seen from the Earth, from the Sun, or both.

range.description: Candidate dates. Default (datetime reference only): the longest window the caps allow, up to 100 years in the chosen direction (50 on each side for 'both').

reference.description: The sky to match: 'now' (default; the current UTC hour or day, echoed in result.reference.date_utc), a UTC moment ('2026-10-29T00:00Z' or 'YYYY-MM-DD'), {datetime: ...}, or your own configuration {values: {feature id: value}}. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

require_same_retrograde.description: Keep only dates whose retrograde flags equal the reference's.

resolution.description: Step of the candidate grid. At most 36,600 candidate dates per call, and at most 660,000 dates x ephemeris series (one per body and perspective, plus one per retrograde-flagged body).

weights.description: Optional {feature id: weight}, default 1 each, e.g. {'geo.jupiter': 2}. Feature ids: '<geo|helio>.<body>' (longitude, 0-360), '<geo|helio>.<a>-<b>:angle' (separation, 0-180), '<geo|helio>.<body>:declination' (degrees) and 'geo.<body>:retrograde' (true/false).

name: sky_analogues

endpoint.description: The REST route that computed it, e.g. 'western/natal'.

deterministic.description: Always true: same input, same result.

llm_used.description: Always false: no language model is involved.

payment.description: How this call was paid: protocol ('free' or 'none'), price and the free calls remaining.

reproducibility.description: How to reproduce and check this result.

result_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical 'result'; check it with verify_result_hash.

counts.description: Number of candidate dates, eligible dates and matches.

matches.description: Matching dates ranked by score: 'columns' format = {rank: [...], date_utc: [...], timestamp: [...], score: [...], <body or feature>: [...], distance:<feature id>: [...]}; 'rows' format = one object per match.

reference.description: The reference sky: its date_utc and timestamp with every body's longitude and retrograde flag (and matched angles / declinations), or the values you gave.

settings.description: Settings applied: reference source, direction, range, resolution, perspectives, bodies, features and their ids, weights, top_n, max_distance, min_separation_days, zodiac, frames, column names and the metric definition (formula per feature).

title: Sky analogues (matching skies)
